On July 6, 2016, Wade announced that he was leaving the Heat to go join his hometown [Chicago Bulls](/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls").[[31]](#cite_note-31)

In September 2016, Bosh failed his physical exam with the Heat and was not cleared by the team to participate in training camp.[[32]](#cite_note-32)[[33]](#cite_note-33) On September 26, 2016, Heat president Riley said he viewed Bosh's career with the team as over, noting that the team was no longer working toward his return.[[34]](#cite_note-34) On July 4, 2017, the Heat waived Bosh a month after an NBA ruling declared his blood clotting issues a career-ending illness.[[35]](#cite_note-BoshWaived-35)[[36]](#cite_note-36) Riley immediately announced that Bosh's number would be retired in the future out of respect to him and his accomplishments with the Heat.[[35]](#cite_note-BoshWaived-35) With nearly all remnants of the Big Three era gone in just two seasons, Miami went 41–41 and missed the playoffs by virtue of a tiebreaker with the Chicago Bulls.

Also during that off-season, the Heat would select [Bam Adebayo](/wiki/Bam_Adebayo "Bam Adebayo") during the [2017 NBA draft](/wiki/2017_NBA_draft "2017 NBA draft") and on February 8, 2018, the Miami Heat would acquire Dwyane Wade back from the Cleveland Cavaliers.[[37]](#cite_note-37) Wade willed the Heat to a game two win against the Philadelphia 76ers in the first round of the [2018 playoffs](/wiki/2018_NBA_playoffs "2018 NBA playoffs"), but the team would lose the series in five games. Wade retired after one last season with the Heat in [2018–19](/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_NBA_season "2018–19 NBA season"); Bosh and Wade's jerseys were retired in March 2019 and February 2020, respectively.
